---
title: "BGE Discovery MCs: System Load vs. PJM Zone Load"
reference-location: margin
fig-cap-location: bottom
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

This notebook re-computes BGE's hourly delivery marginal costs (bulk
transmission and distribution + sub-transmission) using **BGE's own total
system load** from the discovery response instead of the PJM zone hourly demand
used in the production pipeline. The goal is to see how the peak-hour
identification — and therefore the shape of the 8760 marginal cost signal —
changes when we substitute the utility's actual system load for the ISO zone
load.

**What stays the same:** The annual `$/kW-yr` cost values (blended NITS rate
for bulk TX, CPI-inflated Brattle avoided cost for dist/sub-TX) and the
allocation parameters (K=150 for bulk TX, K=100 for dist/sub-TX). Only the
hourly load profile used to identify peak hours changes.

**What changes:** Which hours are selected as "peak" and how cost is
distributed across those hours, since BGE's system load may peak at different
times than the PJM zone load series.

## Setup

```{python}
#| label: setup

from __future__ import annotations

import io

import boto3
import polars as pl

from lib.plotnine import SB_COLORS, theme_switchbox
from lib.quarto import display_figure
from lib.rates_analysis.rate_case_funcs import (
    load_delivery_mc_heatmap,
    plot_mc_heatmap,
)
```

## Parameters

```{python}
#| label: params

STATE = "MD"
UTILITY = "bge"
YEAR = 2025

K_BULK_TX = 150
K_DIST_SUB_TX = 100

print(f"state={STATE}  utility={UTILITY}  year={YEAR}")
print(f"Bulk TX: K={K_BULK_TX}  |  Dist/sub-TX: K={K_DIST_SUB_TX}")
```

## Load production MCs (baseline)

These are the 8760 marginal costs generated by the production pipeline using
PJM zone hourly demand as the peak-identification profile.

```{python}
#| label: load-production

mc_prod = load_delivery_mc_heatmap(STATE, UTILITY, YEAR)
print(f"Production MCs: {mc_prod.height:,} hours, columns: {mc_prod.columns}")

ANNUAL_BULK_TX = float(mc_prod["mc_bulk_tx"].sum())
ANNUAL_DIST_SUB_TX = float(mc_prod["mc_dist_sub_tx"].sum())
print(f"\nAnnual $/kW-yr (from production parquets):")
print(f"  Bulk TX:      ${ANNUAL_BULK_TX:.6f}")
print(f"  Dist/sub-TX:  ${ANNUAL_DIST_SUB_TX:.6f}")
```

## Load BGE discovery system load

The discovery response file `bge_hourly_residential_kwh.xlsx` contains BGE's
total system load for calendar year 2024 (column `System Load`, in kWh). This
is 8,784 hours (2024 is a leap year). We drop Feb 29 to get 8,760 hours and
remap timestamps to 2025 so the heatmaps are directly comparable.

```{python}
#| label: load-discovery

_s3 = boto3.client("s3")
_obj = _s3.get_object(
    Bucket="data.sb",
    Key="bge/bge_hourly_residential_kwh.xlsx",
)
_raw = pl.read_excel(io.BytesIO(_obj["Body"].read()))

bge_load = (
    _raw.filter(pl.col("System Load").is_not_null())
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("Day")
        .cast(pl.String)
        .str.zfill(6)
        .str.to_datetime("%m%d%y")
        .alias("date"),
    )
    .select(
        pl.col("date"),
        pl.col("Hour").cast(pl.Int32).alias("hour_ending"),
        pl.col("System Load").alias("load_kwh"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        (
            pl.col("date")
            + pl.duration(hours=pl.col("hour_ending").cast(pl.Int64) - 1)
        ).alias("timestamp"),
    )
)

print(f"Raw discovery load: {bge_load.height:,} hours")
print(f"Date range: {bge_load['date'].min()} – {bge_load['date'].max()}")
```

Drop Feb 29 (leap year) and remap timestamps from 2024 to 2025:

```{python}
#| label: normalize-discovery

bge_8760 = (
    bge_load.filter(
        ~(
            (pl.col("timestamp").dt.month() == 2)
            & (pl.col("timestamp").dt.day() == 29)
        )
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.offset_by("1y").alias("timestamp"),
    )
    .sort("timestamp")
)

assert bge_8760.height == 8760, f"Expected 8760 hours, got {bge_8760.height}"
print(f"Normalized: {bge_8760.height:,} hours")
print(f"Timestamp range: {bge_8760['timestamp'].min()} – {bge_8760['timestamp'].max()}")
print(f"\nLoad stats (kWh):")
print(f"  Min:  {bge_8760['load_kwh'].min():,.0f}")
print(f"  Max:  {bge_8760['load_kwh'].max():,.0f}")
print(f"  Mean: {bge_8760['load_kwh'].mean():,.0f}")
```

Let's look at the first few rows to confirm the data looks right:

```{python}
#| label: show-discovery

bge_8760.select("timestamp", "load_kwh").head(10)
```

## Validate discovery load against PJM zonal demand

Before using the discovery system load to re-allocate marginal costs, let's
verify it represents the same quantity as the PJM hourly metered demand for the
BGE zone (zone BC) that the production pipeline uses. Both should be BGE's
total system load for 2024; if they match, we can be confident that the
discovery data is a valid substitute load profile.

The PJM data is in MW (average power over the hour); the discovery data is in
kWh (energy over the hour). For a 1-hour interval, kWh ÷ 1,000 = MW.

```{python}
#| label: load-pjm-2024

pjm_2024 = pl.read_parquet(
    "s3://data.sb/pjm/hourly_demand/utilities/utility=bge/year=2024/",
    hive_partitioning=True,
    storage_options={"aws_region": "us-west-2"},
).sort("timestamp")

print(f"PJM 2024 BGE zonal demand: {pjm_2024.height:,} hours")
print(f"Columns: {pjm_2024.columns}")
print(f"Date range: {pjm_2024['timestamp'].min()} – {pjm_2024['timestamp'].max()}")
print(f"\nLoad stats (MW):")
print(f"  Min:  {pjm_2024['load_mw'].min():.1f}")
print(f"  Max:  {pjm_2024['load_mw'].max():.1f}")
print(f"  Mean: {pjm_2024['load_mw'].mean():.1f}")
```

Join the two series on timestamp. PJM timestamps are tz-aware
(`America/New_York`); the discovery timestamps are tz-naive, so we strip the
timezone from PJM before joining.

```{python}
#| label: compare-loads

comparison = (
    bge_load.select("timestamp", pl.col("load_kwh").alias("discovery_kwh"))
    .join(
        pjm_2024.select(
            pl.col("timestamp").dt.replace_time_zone(None).alias("timestamp"),
            pl.col("load_mw").alias("pjm_mw"),
        ),
        on="timestamp",
        how="inner",
    )
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("discovery_kwh") / 1000).alias("discovery_mw"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("discovery_mw") - pl.col("pjm_mw")).alias("delta_mw"),
        (
            (pl.col("discovery_mw") - pl.col("pjm_mw"))
            / pl.col("pjm_mw")
            * 100
        ).alias("delta_pct"),
    )
    .sort("timestamp")
)

print(f"Matched hours: {comparison.height:,} / {bge_load.height:,} discovery, {pjm_2024.height:,} PJM")
print(f"\n{'=' * 55}")
print("LOAD COMPARISON: discovery − PJM")
print(f"{'=' * 55}")
print(f"  Mean delta:    {comparison['delta_mw'].mean():+.1f} MW")
print(f"  Median delta:  {comparison['delta_mw'].median():+.1f} MW")
print(f"  Std delta:     {comparison['delta_mw'].std():.1f} MW")
print(f"  Min delta:     {comparison['delta_mw'].min():+.1f} MW")
print(f"  Max delta:     {comparison['delta_mw'].max():+.1f} MW")
print(f"\n  Mean |delta|:  {comparison['delta_mw'].abs().mean():.1f} MW")
print(f"  Mean |delta%|: {comparison['delta_pct'].abs().mean():.2f}%")
print(f"\n  Pearson r:     {float(comparison.select(pl.corr('discovery_mw', 'pjm_mw')).item()):.6f}")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-load-scatter
#| fig-cap: "BGE discovery system load vs. PJM zonal demand (2024, hourly). Points on the dashed 45° line indicate identical values."

import plotnine as p9

_p = (
    p9.ggplot(comparison, p9.aes("pjm_mw", "discovery_mw"))
    + p9.geom_point(alpha=0.08, size=0.5, color=SB_COLORS["midnight"])
    + p9.geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1, color=SB_COLORS["carrot"], linetype="dashed")
    + p9.labs(
        title="BGE Discovery System Load vs. PJM Zonal Demand (2024)",
        x="PJM zonal demand (MW)",
        y="Discovery system load (MW)",
    )
    + theme_switchbox()
    + p9.theme(figure_size=(7, 7))
)
display_figure(_p.draw())
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-delta-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Hourly load difference (discovery − PJM, MW) by day of year and hour. Blue = discovery lower; orange = discovery higher."

_delta_hm = comparison.with_columns(
    pl.col("timestamp").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),
    pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("hour"),
)

_p = (
    p9.ggplot(_delta_hm, p9.aes(x="day_of_year", y="hour", fill="delta_mw"))
    + p9.geom_tile()
    + p9.scale_fill_gradient2(
        low=SB_COLORS["sky"],
        mid="#FFFFFF",
        high=SB_COLORS["carrot"],
        midpoint=0,
    )
    + p9.scale_x_continuous(
        breaks=[1, 91, 182, 274, 365],
        labels=["Jan", "Apr", "Jul", "Oct", "Dec"],
        limits=(1, 366),
    )
    + p9.scale_y_continuous(breaks=[0, 6, 12, 18, 23], limits=(0, 23))
    + p9.coord_cartesian(expand=False)
    + p9.labs(
        title="Load Delta: Discovery − PJM (MW)",
        x="",
        y="Hour of day",
        fill="MW",
    )
    + theme_switchbox()
    + p9.theme(figure_size=(10.5, 4), legend_position="right")
)
display_figure(_p.draw())
```

```{python}
#| label: top-divergent-hours

_top_divergent = (
    comparison.sort(pl.col("delta_mw").abs(), descending=True)
    .head(10)
    .select("timestamp", "pjm_mw", "discovery_mw", "delta_mw", "delta_pct")
)

print("Top 10 hours by absolute delta:")
_top_divergent
```

## Re-allocate bulk TX using BGE system load

We apply the same PCAF (Peak Capacity Allocation Factor) logic used by the
production pipeline: rank all 8,760 hours by load, select the top K=150, and
allocate the annual `$/kW-yr` proportionally to each peak hour's share of total
peak-hour load.

```{python}
#| label: allocate-bulk-tx

_top_k_tx = bge_8760.sort("load_kwh", descending=True).head(K_BULK_TX)
_total_peak_load_tx = float(_top_k_tx["load_kwh"].sum())

_allocated_tx = _top_k_tx.with_columns(
    (pl.col("load_kwh") / _total_peak_load_tx * ANNUAL_BULK_TX).alias(
        "mc_bulk_tx"
    )
).select("timestamp", "mc_bulk_tx")

_ref_8760 = bge_8760.select("timestamp")
disc_bulk_tx = (
    _ref_8760.join(_allocated_tx, on="timestamp", how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("mc_bulk_tx").fill_null(0.0))
    .sort("timestamp")
)

_actual_sum_tx = float(disc_bulk_tx["mc_bulk_tx"].sum())
_n_nonzero_tx = disc_bulk_tx.filter(pl.col("mc_bulk_tx") > 0).height
print(f"Bulk TX (BGE system load):")
print(f"  Annual sum: ${_actual_sum_tx:.6f}/kW-yr (expected ${ANNUAL_BULK_TX:.6f})")
print(f"  Non-zero hours: {_n_nonzero_tx} (expected {K_BULK_TX})")
print(f"  Error: ${abs(_actual_sum_tx - ANNUAL_BULK_TX):.8f}")
```

## Re-allocate dist/sub-TX using BGE system load

Same PoP (Probability of Peak) logic, but with K=100 for the distribution +
sub-transmission component.

```{python}
#| label: allocate-dist-sub-tx

_top_k_dist = bge_8760.sort("load_kwh", descending=True).head(K_DIST_SUB_TX)
_total_peak_load_dist = float(_top_k_dist["load_kwh"].sum())

_allocated_dist = _top_k_dist.with_columns(
    (pl.col("load_kwh") / _total_peak_load_dist * ANNUAL_DIST_SUB_TX).alias(
        "mc_dist_sub_tx"
    )
).select("timestamp", "mc_dist_sub_tx")

disc_dist_sub_tx = (
    _ref_8760.join(_allocated_dist, on="timestamp", how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("mc_dist_sub_tx").fill_null(0.0))
    .sort("timestamp")
)

_actual_sum_dist = float(disc_dist_sub_tx["mc_dist_sub_tx"].sum())
_n_nonzero_dist = disc_dist_sub_tx.filter(pl.col("mc_dist_sub_tx") > 0).height
print(f"Dist/sub-TX (BGE system load):")
print(f"  Annual sum: ${_actual_sum_dist:.6f}/kW-yr (expected ${ANNUAL_DIST_SUB_TX:.6f})")
print(f"  Non-zero hours: {_n_nonzero_dist} (expected {K_DIST_SUB_TX})")
print(f"  Error: ${abs(_actual_sum_dist - ANNUAL_DIST_SUB_TX):.8f}")
```

        pl.col("timestamp").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),

print(f"Discovery MC DataFrame: {mc_disc.height:,} rows, columns: {mc_disc.columns}")
mc_disc.head(5)

## Summary comparison

How many peak hours overlap between the PJM zone load and BGE system load
selections? And how does the seasonal distribution shift?

```{python}
#| label: summary-comparison

_SUMMER_MONTHS = {5, 6, 7, 8, 9}

prod_tx_peak_ts = set(
    mc_prod.filter(pl.col("mc_bulk_tx") > 0)["timestamp"].to_list()
)
disc_tx_peak_ts = set(
    mc_disc.filter(pl.col("mc_bulk_tx") > 0)["timestamp"].to_list()
)
tx_overlap = prod_tx_peak_ts & disc_tx_peak_ts

prod_dist_peak_ts = set(
    mc_prod.filter(pl.col("mc_dist_sub_tx") > 0)["timestamp"].to_list()
)
disc_dist_peak_ts = set(
    mc_disc.filter(pl.col("mc_dist_sub_tx") > 0)["timestamp"].to_list()
)
dist_overlap = prod_dist_peak_ts & disc_dist_peak_ts


def _pct_summer(timestamps: set) -> float:
    if not timestamps:
        return 0.0
    summer = sum(1 for ts in timestamps if ts.month in _SUMMER_MONTHS)
    return summer / len(timestamps)


print("=" * 60)
print("PEAK-HOUR OVERLAP")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"\nBulk TX (K={K_BULK_TX}):")
print(f"  Production peak hours: {len(prod_tx_peak_ts)}")
print(f"  Discovery peak hours:  {len(disc_tx_peak_ts)}")
print(f"  Overlap:               {len(tx_overlap)} ({len(tx_overlap)/K_BULK_TX:.0%})")

print(f"\nDist/sub-TX (K={K_DIST_SUB_TX}):")
print(f"  Production peak hours: {len(prod_dist_peak_ts)}")
print(f"  Discovery peak hours:  {len(disc_dist_peak_ts)}")
print(f"  Overlap:               {len(dist_overlap)} ({len(dist_overlap)/K_DIST_SUB_TX:.0%})")

print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("SEASONAL DISTRIBUTION (% of peak hours in May–Sep)")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"\nBulk TX:")
print(f"  Production (PJM zone):   {_pct_summer(prod_tx_peak_ts):.1%}")
print(f"  Discovery (BGE system):  {_pct_summer(disc_tx_peak_ts):.1%}")

print(f"\nDist/sub-TX:")
print(f"  Production (PJM zone):   {_pct_summer(prod_dist_peak_ts):.1%}")
print(f"  Discovery (BGE system):  {_pct_summer(disc_dist_peak_ts):.1%}")

print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("ANNUAL COST VALIDATION (should be identical)")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"\nBulk TX:")
print(f"  Production: ${float(mc_prod['mc_bulk_tx'].sum()):.6f}/kW-yr")
print(f"  Discovery:  ${float(mc_disc['mc_bulk_tx'].sum()):.6f}/kW-yr")

print(f"\nDist/sub-TX:")
print(f"  Production: ${float(mc_prod['mc_dist_sub_tx'].sum()):.6f}/kW-yr")
print(f"  Discovery:  ${float(mc_disc['mc_dist_sub_tx'].sum()):.6f}/kW-yr")
```

## 5-year average load profile (2021–2025)

Instead of using a single year's load shape to identify peak hours, we can
average BGE's hourly zonal demand over the five most recent calendar years
(2021–2025) to produce a "typical year" profile that smooths out year-specific
weather extremes. We then apply the same PCAF/PoP allocation to this averaged
profile.

This is **Option A**: average the 8,760 load values first (one mean per
calendar position across years), then select the top-K hours from the result.
The annual `$/kW-yr` cost values stay the same — only the load profile used to
identify peak hours changes.

We use `scan_parquet` with hive partitioning and predicate pushdown so Polars
only reads the five requested year-partitions from S3, groups by (month, day,
hour) lazily, and collects a single 8,760-row result.

```{python}
#| label: build-avg-profile

AVG_YEARS = list(range(2021, 2026))

avg_profile = (
    pl.scan_parquet(
        "s3://data.sb/pjm/hourly_demand/utilities/utility=bge/",
        hive_partitioning=True,
        storage_options={"aws_region": "us-west-2"},
    )
    .filter(pl.col("year").is_in(AVG_YEARS))
    .with_columns(pl.col("timestamp").dt.replace_time_zone(None))
    .filter(
        ~(
            (pl.col("timestamp").dt.month() == 2)
            & (pl.col("timestamp").dt.day() == 29)
        )
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.month().alias("m"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.day().alias("d"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("h"),
    )
    .group_by("m", "d", "h")
    .agg(
        pl.col("load_mw").mean().alias("load_mw"),
        pl.col("load_mw").count().alias("n_obs"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.datetime(2025, pl.col("m"), pl.col("d"), pl.col("h")).alias("timestamp"),
    )
    .sort("timestamp")
    .collect()
)

assert avg_profile.height == 8760, f"Expected 8760 hours, got {avg_profile.height}"
_min_obs = avg_profile["n_obs"].min()
_max_obs = avg_profile["n_obs"].max()
print(
    f"Average profile: {avg_profile.height:,} hours from "
    f"{len(AVG_YEARS)} years ({AVG_YEARS[0]}–{AVG_YEARS[-1]})"
)
print(f"Observations per position: {_min_obs}–{_max_obs}")
print(f"\nLoad stats (MW):")
print(f"  Min:  {avg_profile['load_mw'].min():.1f}")
print(f"  Max:  {avg_profile['load_mw'].max():.1f}")
print(f"  Mean: {avg_profile['load_mw'].mean():.1f}")
```

### Allocate bulk TX (5-year average)

```{python}
#| label: allocate-bulk-tx-avg

_top_k_tx = avg_profile.sort("load_mw", descending=True).head(K_BULK_TX)
_total_peak = float(_top_k_tx["load_mw"].sum())

_allocated = _top_k_tx.with_columns(
    (pl.col("load_mw") / _total_peak * ANNUAL_BULK_TX).alias("mc_bulk_tx")
).select("timestamp", "mc_bulk_tx")

_ref = avg_profile.select("timestamp")
avg_bulk_tx = (
    _ref.join(_allocated, on="timestamp", how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("mc_bulk_tx").fill_null(0.0))
    .sort("timestamp")
)

_sum = float(avg_bulk_tx["mc_bulk_tx"].sum())
_n = avg_bulk_tx.filter(pl.col("mc_bulk_tx") > 0).height
print(f"Bulk TX (5-year average):")
print(f"  Annual sum: ${_sum:.6f}/kW-yr (expected ${ANNUAL_BULK_TX:.6f})")
print(f"  Non-zero hours: {_n} (expected {K_BULK_TX})")
```

### Allocate dist/sub-TX (5-year average)

```{python}
#| label: allocate-dist-sub-tx-avg

_top_k_dist = avg_profile.sort("load_mw", descending=True).head(K_DIST_SUB_TX)
_total_peak = float(_top_k_dist["load_mw"].sum())

_allocated = _top_k_dist.with_columns(
    (pl.col("load_mw") / _total_peak * ANNUAL_DIST_SUB_TX).alias("mc_dist_sub_tx")
).select("timestamp", "mc_dist_sub_tx")

avg_dist_sub_tx = (
    _ref.join(_allocated, on="timestamp", how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("mc_dist_sub_tx").fill_null(0.0))
    .sort("timestamp")
)

_sum = float(avg_dist_sub_tx["mc_dist_sub_tx"].sum())
_n = avg_dist_sub_tx.filter(pl.col("mc_dist_sub_tx") > 0).height
print(f"Dist/sub-TX (5-year average):")
print(f"  Annual sum: ${_sum:.6f}/kW-yr (expected ${ANNUAL_DIST_SUB_TX:.6f})")
print(f"  Non-zero hours: {_n} (expected {K_DIST_SUB_TX})")
```

        on="timestamp",
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),

## 10-year average load profile (2016–2025)

Same approach as the 5-year average, but using ten calendar years (2016–2025)
for a longer baseline that captures more winter variability.

```{python}
#| label: build-avg10-profile

AVG_YEARS_10 = list(range(2016, 2026))

avg10_profile = (
    pl.scan_parquet(
        "s3://data.sb/pjm/hourly_demand/utilities/utility=bge/",
        hive_partitioning=True,
        storage_options={"aws_region": "us-west-2"},
    )
    .filter(pl.col("year").is_in(AVG_YEARS_10))
    .with_columns(pl.col("timestamp").dt.replace_time_zone(None))
    .filter(
        ~(
            (pl.col("timestamp").dt.month() == 2)
            & (pl.col("timestamp").dt.day() == 29)
        )
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.month().alias("m"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.day().alias("d"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("h"),
    )
    .group_by("m", "d", "h")
    .agg(
        pl.col("load_mw").mean().alias("load_mw"),
        pl.col("load_mw").count().alias("n_obs"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.datetime(2025, pl.col("m"), pl.col("d"), pl.col("h")).alias("timestamp"),
    )
    .sort("timestamp")
    .collect()
)

assert avg10_profile.height == 8760, f"Expected 8760 hours, got {avg10_profile.height}"
_min_obs = avg10_profile["n_obs"].min()
_max_obs = avg10_profile["n_obs"].max()
print(
    f"Average profile: {avg10_profile.height:,} hours from "
    f"{len(AVG_YEARS_10)} years ({AVG_YEARS_10[0]}–{AVG_YEARS_10[-1]})"
)
print(f"Observations per position: {_min_obs}–{_max_obs}")
print(f"\nLoad stats (MW):")
print(f"  Min:  {avg10_profile['load_mw'].min():.1f}")
print(f"  Max:  {avg10_profile['load_mw'].max():.1f}")
print(f"  Mean: {avg10_profile['load_mw'].mean():.1f}")
```

### Allocate bulk TX (10-year average)

```{python}
#| label: allocate-bulk-tx-avg10

_top_k_tx = avg10_profile.sort("load_mw", descending=True).head(K_BULK_TX)
_total_peak = float(_top_k_tx["load_mw"].sum())

_allocated = _top_k_tx.with_columns(
    (pl.col("load_mw") / _total_peak * ANNUAL_BULK_TX).alias("mc_bulk_tx")
).select("timestamp", "mc_bulk_tx")

_ref10 = avg10_profile.select("timestamp")
avg10_bulk_tx = (
    _ref10.join(_allocated, on="timestamp", how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("mc_bulk_tx").fill_null(0.0))
    .sort("timestamp")
)

_sum = float(avg10_bulk_tx["mc_bulk_tx"].sum())
_n = avg10_bulk_tx.filter(pl.col("mc_bulk_tx") > 0).height
print(f"Bulk TX (10-year average):")
print(f"  Annual sum: ${_sum:.6f}/kW-yr (expected ${ANNUAL_BULK_TX:.6f})")
print(f"  Non-zero hours: {_n} (expected {K_BULK_TX})")
```

### Allocate dist/sub-TX (10-year average)

```{python}
#| label: allocate-dist-sub-tx-avg10

_top_k_dist = avg10_profile.sort("load_mw", descending=True).head(K_DIST_SUB_TX)
_total_peak = float(_top_k_dist["load_mw"].sum())

_allocated = _top_k_dist.with_columns(
    (pl.col("load_mw") / _total_peak * ANNUAL_DIST_SUB_TX).alias("mc_dist_sub_tx")
).select("timestamp", "mc_dist_sub_tx")

avg10_dist_sub_tx = (
    _ref10.join(_allocated, on="timestamp", how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("mc_dist_sub_tx").fill_null(0.0))
    .sort("timestamp")
)

_sum = float(avg10_dist_sub_tx["mc_dist_sub_tx"].sum())
_n = avg10_dist_sub_tx.filter(pl.col("mc_dist_sub_tx") > 0).height
print(f"Dist/sub-TX (10-year average):")
print(f"  Annual sum: ${_sum:.6f}/kW-yr (expected ${ANNUAL_DIST_SUB_TX:.6f})")
print(f"  Non-zero hours: {_n} (expected {K_DIST_SUB_TX})")
```

### Combine and visualize

```{python}
#| label: combine-avg10

mc_avg10 = (
    avg10_bulk_tx.join(
        avg10_dist_sub_tx.select("timestamp", "mc_dist_sub_tx"),
        on="timestamp",
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("hour"),
    )
    .sort("timestamp")
)

print(f"10-year average MC DataFrame: {mc_avg10.height:,} rows")
```

print(f"  Discovery (2024 BGE system):   {_pct_summer(disc_tx_peak_ts):.1%}")

print(f"  10-year average (2016–2025):   {_pct_summer(avg10_tx_peak_ts):.1%}")

print(f"\nDist/sub-TX (K={K_DIST_SUB_TX}):")

print(f"  10-year average (2016–2025):   {_pct_summer(avg10_dist_peak_ts):.1%}")

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("WINTER HOURS (Nov–Mar) IN PEAK SET")
print("=" * 70)

_WINTER_MONTHS = {1, 2, 3, 11, 12}


def _pct_winter(timestamps: set) -> float:
    if not timestamps:
        return 0.0
    winter = sum(1 for ts in timestamps if ts.month in _WINTER_MONTHS)
    return winter / len(timestamps)


print(f"\nBulk TX (K={K_BULK_TX}):")
print(f"  Production (2025 PJM zone):    {_pct_winter(prod_tx_peak_ts):.1%}")
print(f"  Discovery (2024 BGE system):   {_pct_winter(disc_tx_peak_ts):.1%}")
print(f"  5-year average (2021–2025):    {_pct_winter(avg_tx_peak_ts):.1%}")
print(f"  10-year average (2016–2025):   {_pct_winter(avg10_tx_peak_ts):.1%}")

print(f"\nDist/sub-TX (K={K_DIST_SUB_TX}):")
print(f"  Production (2025 PJM zone):    {_pct_winter(prod_dist_peak_ts):.1%}")
print(f"  Discovery (2024 BGE system):   {_pct_winter(disc_dist_peak_ts):.1%}")
print(f"  5-year average (2021–2025):    {_pct_winter(avg_dist_peak_ts):.1%}")
print(f"  10-year average (2016–2025):   {_pct_winter(avg10_dist_peak_ts):.1%}")

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
